comparator.name: Political Science: International Relations and Organisations (IRO)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current IRO catalogue and regulations establish 60 EC in each year. Year two has eleven required 5 EC courses and a choice of Contemporary Political Philosophy or Rational Choice Theory. The current catalogue uses 6442HASRBY for Academic Skills: Research Design where the annex lists 6442HASRDY. Year three has a 10 EC seminar, 20 EC Bachelor Project and 30 EC of approved open study. Political Leadership is one seminar example. The seminar requires the first year, and the project also requires 40 EC from year two including Research Design, Statistics II and Qualitative Research Methods. The project combines subject instruction with an individual thesis based on original research. The module assigns 40% to the subject assignments and 60% to the thesis, which must pass separately. The elective space needs approval; a research internship may count for 15 EC and has separate entry requirements.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names International Relations and Organisations (IRO), which Leiden confirms as a current formal direction in the Political Science bachelor. The exact IRO route is reconstructed; the separate National and International Politics direction is not combined with it.

core: Power, actors, conflict and cooperation in international relations
European Union politics and regional governance
International political economy, development and environmental politics
Comparative politics, democracy and political systems
Public policy, institutions and political decision-making
Global history and the historical context of political change
Quantitative political research, statistics and data analysis
Qualitative political research and research design
Academic writing, argumentation and communication about politics
adjacent: International security, international law, human rights and data-informed global governance
Diplomacy, international organisations and policy analysis as further-study and career directions
questions: Why do states and other political actors cooperate, compete and go to war?
How can political science explain current international events beyond headlines?
How do globalisation, human rights, media and public opinion shape international politics?

alternatives.label: International Relations, Organisations and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: International relations, comparative politics and European integration provide the core. Economics and environmental policy and communication add breadth.
alternatives.concept: Study how states and international organisations cooperate, compete and make rules. Combine international relations, comparative politics and EU governance with economics, sustainability governance and persuasive communication. Use quantitative and qualitative methods to investigate political and economic questions.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Research Methods & Statistics precede the courses that require them. Political foundations lead to international relations, EU politics, sustainability governance and peace and conflict.

alternatives.label: International Security, Law and Global Governance
alternatives.labelReason: Peace and conflict, international and criminal law, military history and youth resilience organise the security emphasis. Data science and historical research add different ways to investigate it.
alternatives.concept: Study conflict, peacebuilding and international law alongside the institutions that govern across borders. Examine the history of warfare, criminal liability and youth radicalisation from their respective disciplines. Use historical research, qualitative inquiry and data analysis to investigate questions about governance and security.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Research Methods & Statistics precede the courses that require them. Introduction to Data Science precedes Machine Learning, and Modern History and History of Empires precede the research seminar.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses differ in each direction. The security option adds criminal law, warfare, youth resilience, historical research and two data science courses. The broader option adds microeconomics, public economics, persuasive communication, sustainability governance, introductory sociology and rhetoric.

selection.assessment: Exact IRO curriculum and module evidence establishes the comparison. Inherited interests provide discovery context. Two feasible options share eighteen courses and differ in six. The broad route combines international politics and open-economy analysis with sustainability governance and persuasive communication. The security route adds criminal law, warfare, youth resilience, historical research and data science. A third political economy and EU governance route would repeat the broad option’s economics, EU politics and EU law without a separate disciplinary progression.

blocks: International relations, comparative politics and political theory
Both examine political theory and normative questions; UCR introduces major traditions rather than Leiden’s contemporary advanced course.
Both establish comparative-politics concepts and methods for analysing political systems.
Both analyse international-relations theories and their use in explaining state behaviour.
The selected Leiden bachelor seminar is a dedicated advanced study of political leadership in international relations; no scheduled UCR course reproduces that seminar.
Introduction to Political Science is a separately credited disciplinary foundation; the selected UCR politics courses divide that foundation across specialised courses and cannot be matched twice.
Both provide historical context for contemporary international politics; UCR focuses on modern global history.
International organisations, security, EU politics and law
Public international law is a central legal architecture of international organisations; UCR approaches the institutions through law.
Both directly examine international security, conflict and responses to political violence.
Both examine European Union institutions, decision-making and politics.
Both address human rights and international legal order, with UCR integrating legal and philosophical perspectives.
Both compare political and constitutional systems; UCR approaches the comparison through constitutional law.
Both establish economic principles needed for political-economy analysis.
Both study international economic relations. UCR emphasizes open-economy macroeconomic models, while Leiden examines the politics of the international economy.
Leiden requires a dedicated International Development course; no scheduled UCR course reproduces its political-science framing.
Both examine how political institutions and actors respond to environmental problems. UCR focuses on governance of sustainability.
Both introduce research design, operationalisation, sampling and empirical analysis.
Econometrics develops estimators and hypothesis testing relevant to Leiden’s second statistics course.
Both train qualitative research design and methods in social and political inquiry.
Both require students to frame a question and design research. UCR applies historical methods to the American Century, while Leiden trains political science research design.
UCR’s Research Methods & Statistics course is already matched to Leiden’s introductory research-methods unit and cannot separately reproduce Statistics I.
Leiden’s integrated qualitative-and-quantitative academic-skills unit has no separate scheduled UCR equivalent.
Both develop argumentation and communication. UCR studies rhetoric, while Leiden applies these skills to actors in world politics.
Leiden combines introductory international relations with academic skills. UCR develops these areas through separate courses.
Leiden requires a 20 EC project with an individual thesis. Optional UCR independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.
This is genuine approved elective, minor, exchange or internship space and has no universal subject content to match.

notes.text: Leiden has dedicated courses in international organisations, development and political science methods, and requires a 10 EC seminar and a 20 EC Bachelor Project with an individual thesis. The UCR options combine related politics, law, economics, history and research methods. Optional UCR independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s International Relations and Organisations programme studies global politics, international institutions, security and development. It develops political science research skills and ends with a seminar and an individual thesis within the Bachelor Project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The two UCR options share international relations, comparative politics, EU politics and law, and research methods. One adds political economy and policy. The other focuses on conflict, security and the institutions that respond to them.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC route includes one 5 EC restricted choice, a 10 EC seminar, a 20 EC Bachelor Project and 30 EC of approved open study.
